chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The best of your women is the one with a pleasant fragrance, skilled in cooking, who when she spends, spends with moderation, and when she refrains, refrains with moderation. Such a woman is a worker from among the workers of God, and a worker of God will neither fail nor be remorseful.

key_terms.الطَّبِيخِ: Cooking — skilled preparation of food, a domestic virtue in classical Arab-Islamic culture
key_terms.الطَّيِّبَةُ الرِّيحِ: Pleasant fragrance — in classical Islamic tradition, cleanliness and pleasant scent were signs of care for one's household and person
key_terms.بِمَعْرُوفٍ: With ma'ruf — with what is recognized as appropriate, moderate, and socially virtuous; a Quranic term for right conduct
key_terms.عَامِلُ اللَّهِ: Worker of God — one who acts in God's service; a remarkable elevation of the pious woman to a divine agent

ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of a good wife according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the ideal qualities of a woman in terms of household excellence and financial wisdom. The emphasis on spending and withholding 'with ma'ruf' (what is recognized as appropriate) echoes Quranic principles of balanced financial conduct. The concluding statement — that a worker of God neither fails nor regrets — elevates the woman who embodies these virtues to a divine role, assuring her of spiritual success.
